Hormuz ship traffic grinds to near halt after US and Iran strikes

📅 2026-07-09 ✍️ Bloomberg (via Insurance Journal) 🏷️ Strait of Hormuz, ship traffic, Mapbox, OpenStreetMap, maritime tracking, Iran, US strikes, oil transit, electronic interference, geopolitical mapping
🔗 Read the source article →

💡 Quick summary

Ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz nearly stopped after US military strikes on Iran, with tracking data powered by Mapbox and OpenStreetMap showing only sanctioned vessels on an Iran-approved route while the Omani corridor went quiet.

📌 Key takeaways

  • Traffic through the Strait of Hormuz came to a near standstill on July 10, 2026, after the US struck Iran for a second consecutive day
  • Only 14 commodity carriers crossed the strait in both directions on Wednesday — the lowest since the interim peace deal in mid-June
  • Observable movements largely followed an Iran-approved route near the waterway's north, while the US-supported Omani corridor was quiet
  • Average daily transits since the mid-June interim deal were 34 commodity vessels, with a peak of 59 on June 24 — compared to fewer than 20 daily during wartime
  • Electronic interference returned, with vessels southeast of Limah showing implausible speeds of 30+ knots, indicating possible defense system activation affecting transponder signals
